rules/projects/webdev-task-template: environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, tests/.dockerignore, tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py (compared byte-for-byte, CR-insensitive, with the task copies)

evidence: Source review of the frozen bytes; no defect found in this row's scope. (1) Agent image ships no grading material: task/environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies only 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/' and 'COPY assets/ /assets/'; it installs only express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (no rewardkit, no judge CLI, no Playwright), and never references tests/ or solution/. The file is identical to the frozen template. (2) Grading is isolated: task.toml:28 'environment_mode = "separate"' with task.toml:2 'artifacts = ["/app", "/assets"]'; tests/Dockerfile:43-44 'COPY . /tests' and 'RUN chmod +x /tests/test.sh && chmod -R go-rwx /tests' exist only in the verifier image. (3) No readable rubric copy in the agent's world: a scan of instruction.md, the six /instructions notes and seed_data.json for judge|rubric|criteri|rewardkit|reward|/tests|/logs|verifier|scoring|gate|likert|weight|playwright|grader|placeholders returned zero hits, and none of the 55 criterion ids from the five judge.toml files appears in any agent-visible file; seed_data.json is 149 bytes with an empty snippets list. (4) The submission cannot write or read the reward at grading time: tests/test.sh:3 'umask 077', :11 'chmod 700 "$LOG_DIR"', :12 'chmod -R go-rwx /tests', and :104-111 launch the app with 'setsid env -i ... setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups node "$APP_ENTRY"', so the app process has no ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/OPENROUTER key in its environment and no access to /tests or /logs/verifier; test.sh:72-83 refuses any symlink in /app that is not inside /app/node_modules resolving inside /app/node_modules, which blocks pointing a submitted file at /tests or /logs. The key exists only as the template '${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}' in [verifier.env] (task.toml:34), never in the agent phase. (5) Shared files test.sh, tests/Dockerfile, .dockerignore, scoring.toml, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py are identical to the frozen template (diff after CR stripping: SAME for all seven compared files), so no task-specific weakening exists. (6) solution/solve.sh writes only under /app (grep for /tests|/logs|/solution: no hits) and the golden server.js reads only DB_PATH/SQLITE_PATH/PORT from the environment. (7) All five prompts carry the untrusted-submission line and 'never run shell or install commands'; the functional judge.toml wires only playwright and the single-use verifier restart server. Counterexamples tried: (a) a broken app that tries to read /tests/scored/functional/judge.toml or write /logs/verifier/reward.json from server.js at grading time is stopped by uid 65534 against root-owned mode-700 trees; (b) a submission shipping /app/rubric -> /tests is refused by the symlink loop and scores the pre-written zero; (c) an agent searching its own container finds no /tests, no rewardkit and no criterion text; (d) a conforming app using node_modules/.bin symlinks that stay inside /app/node_modules is not rejected, and integration.md:11 states that rule publicly. Evidence hashes: 18 of 22 indexed artifacts match as stored; the four hosted-run JSON files of run 4e686738 (result.json, verifier/reward.json, verifier/scored/reward-details.json, verifier/gates/reward-details.json) hash differently in the worktree because they are checked out with CRLF (core.autocrlf=true); their LF-normalised SHA256 values match the index (4a9b1934..., bcfe3714..., bacbf94c..., 5b001eb8...). Notes, not defects: N1 no configured-judge or hosted run exists for these exact bytes, so isolation is established from source and from template identity, not from a run; the earlier hosted run (reward.json 0.9833, graded 1) used the same isolation files but a different candidate. N2 the index hashes for those four hosted files are reproducible only on LF bytes; a reviewer hashing the worktree files directly sees a mismatch. N3 residual, template-controlled: the claude-code judge runs as root in the container that holds /tests, so reward integrity against a submission that tries to instruct the judge rests on the prompt-level untrusted-input rule (row 45 scope), not on a filesystem boundary.
